claims.text: The intervention is to add approximately 2 at% Hf to a refractory high-entropy alloy that initially contains no Hf addition.
Approximately 2 at% Hf will produce a uniform distribution of fine Hf-rich precipitates in the alloy matrix.
The Hf-rich precipitates will remain thermally stable up to approximately 1200°C.
Hf addition forms nanoscale precipitates that impede dislocation motion.
Impedance of dislocation motion by the Hf-rich precipitates provides precipitation strengthening at high temperature.
The precipitation-strengthening mechanism will enhance high-temperature yield strength.
The precipitation-strengthening mechanism will enhance creep resistance.
At around 1200°C under tensile or creep loading, the Hf-modified alloy will have greater mechanical strength than the Hf-free baseline.
Approximately 2 at% Hf will increase high-temperature yield strength and creep resistance by roughly 10–25% relative to the Hf-free baseline.
The Hf-modified alloy will retain room-temperature mechanical properties comparable to those of the Hf-free baseline.
The Hf-modified alloy will preserve room-temperature ductility.
Adding approximately 2 at% Hf will cause only a minimal increase in density relative to the baseline.
The predicted benefit is conditional on keeping the Hf concentration near 2 at%.
The predicted benefit is conditional on the Hf-rich precipitates remaining uniformly dispersed and thermally stable up to about 1200°C.
Precipitate coarsening may negate the predicted mechanical benefits.
Hf concentrations above the proposed low level may negate the predicted benefits.
The magnitude of strengthening and the optimal Hf concentration depend on processing variables and may differ among refractory high-entropy alloy formulations.
TEM can be used to test whether the proposed Hf-rich precipitates form and are uniformly distributed.
Less than a 10% improvement in high-temperature yield strength or creep resistance relative to the baseline is specified as a falsifying result.
Significant room-temperature ductility degradation or an unacceptable density increase is specified as a falsifying result.
